chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud, from Yahya ibn Adam, from Shareek, from Jabir ibn Yazeed, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The magnanimity of patience in the state of need and destitution, and abstinence and riches, is greater than the magnanimity of giving.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the magnanimity of patience and the magnanimity of giving charity?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the passive virtue of enduring need with dignity and the active virtue of giving, asserting that self-restraint in poverty requires greater spiritual fortitude than generosity in wealth. This hadith, found in *Al-Kafi*, underscores the Shia emphasis on *hilm* (forbearance) and inner character over external displays of piety. It reflects the broader theological principle that the test of scarcity often reveals deeper sincerity than the ease of abundance.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali Bin Muhammad Al Qasany, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Suleyman Bin Dawood, from Yahya Bin Adam, from Shareek, from Jabir Bin Yazeed, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Magnanimity of exercising the patience during a state of need, and the destitution, and the abstinence, and the riches, is more than the magnanimity (regarding) the giving (charity etc.)’.
en.sarwar: 22. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani fro al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman ibn Dawud form Yahya ibn Adam from Sharik from Jabir ibn Yazid from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said, ‘
The courage to exercise patience in times of need and poverty with chastity and self-sufficiency is more than the courage needed to give charity.’”
